RELS 398.10 / ENGL 398.10 · Digital Methods for Historical Documents

Instructor Lesson & Lab Plan: Meeting #2

Date: Friday, September 4, 2026 Time: 9:30 AM – 10:20 AM (50 mins) Room: Mulroney Hall 3032 (MULH 3032) Pre-requisite: Lesson 1.1 Interactive Completed

🏛️ CORE CURRICULUM DIRECTIVE: FULL-PAGE ARTIFACT SELECTION

The chosen textual witness MUST be an entire full page (folio recto, folio verso, or complete epigraphic surface) of the artifact. Do not allow students to select isolated sentences or verse snippets. A full-page specimen is mathematically required because our downstream modules depend on page-level codicological evidence: bounding margins, ruling patterns (M1), quire structure (M2), multi-spectral IIIF image manifests (M3), full-page HTR baseline recognition (M4), lineation alignment (M6), and apparatus layout (M8).

Class Schedule & Pedagogical Flow (50 Minutes)

Timing Phase & Focus Actionable Instructions & Instructor Cues
09:30 – 09:38
(8 mins)		 1. Welcome & Lesson 1.1 Debrief
Review & Synthesis 		• Pulse Check: Survey students on Wednesday’s interactive lesson on Moodle. Confirm everyone understands why plain text (`.txt`, `.md`, `.xml`) is the foundation of durable scholarship rather than proprietary word processors.
• Concept Anchor: Remind students of Git as a scholarly time machine (audit trail of editorial decisions) and Claude/AI as an inspectable assistant that must always be verified against manuscript evidence.
09:38 – 09:50
(12 mins)		 2. FAIR Principles & The 8-Stage Pipeline
Theory & Architecture 		• FAIR Presentation: Introduce Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable (Wilkinson et al. 2016). Emphasize that FAIR is not administrative compliance; it is what makes digital scholarship cumulative.
• The 8-Stage Semester Journey: Walk through how today’s single manuscript page will travel across every week: Catalogue (W2) → IIIF Manifest (W3) → HTR Transcription (W4) → Reconciliation & Normalization (W5-6) → Collation (W7) → Morphological Markup (W9) → Translation Alignment (W11) → Web Edition (W13).
09:50 – 10:10
(20 mins)		 3. Hands-On Lab: Full-Page Witness Selection
Active Workshop 		• Live Demo: Display live digital manuscript repositories on the projector (e.g., Digita Vaticana, British Library, CSNTM, Gallica).
• Enforce Full-Page Rule: Guide students to identify a single, complete folio (e.g., f. 12v, p. 45).
• Run the 5-Point Quality Check: 1. Image: Minimum 300 DPI or zoomable IIIF viewer.
2. Identifier: Permanent shelfmark (e.g., Vat. gr. 2121, Pinakes ID).
3. Text: Full page containing known text (e.g., complete chapter section or poem).
4. Handwriting: Clean, legible script (avoid heavily degraded palimpsests).
5. Benchmark: Modern printed reference edition available for comparison.
10:10 – 10:17
(7 mins)		 4. Repo Initialization & First FAIR Commit
Technical Practice 		• Create README.md: Students open their local Git course repository in VS Code and write their artifact provenance record.
• Execute Atomic Commit: Students stage, commit, and push their choice:
# In terminal / VS Code command prompt:
git add README.md
git commit -m "Choose full-page witness: Vat. gr. 2121 f. 213r (Gen 1:1-12)"
git push origin main
10:17 – 10:20
(3 mins)		 5. Wrap-Up & Lab Verification
Exit Ticket & Next Week 		• Oxygen Check: Confirm students can launch Oxygen XML Editor on the MULH 3032 lab computers (required for next Wednesday).
• Weekend Reading: Finney (pp. 323–360) and Griffitts §3.4.1 (TEI Header fundamentals).
• Next Tuesday: Hand-authoring our first TEI `` metadata document!

📚 Approved High-Resolution Repositories

  • Digita Vaticana: digi.vatlib.it (Exceptional Greek & Latin codices; native IIIF manifests).
  • British Library Digitised Manuscripts: bl.uk/manuscripts (Cotton, Harley, and Additional collections).
  • CSNTM (Center for New Testament Manuscripts): csntm.org (High-resolution Greek NT minuscules & uncials).
  • Gallica (BnF Paris): gallica.bnf.fr (Vast medieval Greek and European manuscript holdings).
  • Codex Sinaiticus Project: codexsinaiticus.org (High-resolution multi-light alignment).
